confirmed.title: Declared continuation resolved by name alone joins the wrong same-named cluster with no judge
confirmed.claim: continued() returns the latest local whose normalised name equals the `continues` string (line 1334-1336), ignoring kind, ignoring which roster entry the model actually pointed at (the roster_root lookup at 1337-1341 is unreachable, since a roster name is always some member's exact name), and including same-unit siblings (`t["id"] < l["id"]`). unite_on_sight then unites on that target without a settled() check (line 1353). When two rolling clusters carry the same name (different kinds, or judged different), the roster lists both and the new local is welded to whichever bore the name most recently.
confirmed.scenario: Probe run against block 8 with a scripted judge: unit 1 lists Oz (person) and Dorothy; unit 2 lists Oz (place), judge says the two Oz are different (kept_apart); roster now shows two entries named Oz. Unit 3 lists Oz (person, continues "Oz"). Result: ledger row `same declared Oz 2 ~ Oz 3`, clusters [[u1:Oz/person], [u2:Oz/place, u3:Oz/person]] -- the Wizard's unit-3 mentions, facts and cells land on the Land of Oz node, and the same_name path at 1359-1365 cannot repair it because the two clusters are settled. In Oz book 1 the Wizard and the land are both called Oz; in a paper a method and its topic often share a name. Ruling 28's on-sight union is meant for the entity the roster showed, not any local bearing the string.
confirmed.fix: Resolve a declared continuation through the roster entry the model copied: build roster_root as name -> [(root, kind)] in roster_of, prefer the entry whose kind matches l["kind"], skip same-unit locals, and when the name maps to more than one cluster or no kind matches, write the candidate row instead of uniting; also refuse the declared union when state.settled(find(target), find(l)) holds.

verdict.reason: Reproduced by exec-ing blocks 1-8 as the battery does and driving roll_unit with a scripted judge. Unit 1: Oz (person), Dorothy. Unit 2: Oz (place); same_name skips (kind differs), shared_surface nomination judged different -> kept_apart, so roster_of now lists two entries named Oz (roster_text line 890 shows both, with kinds). Unit 3: Oz (person, continues "Oz"); line 1013 accepts the string since it is in roster_names; continued() at lines 1334-1336 returns the latest local named Oz = unit 2's Oz/place, ignoring kind and which roster line the model meant; unite_on_sight line 1353 unites with no settled() check. Ledger row: Oz 2 ~ Oz 3 same declared. Final clusters: [[u1 Oz/person], [u1 Dorothy, u2 Dorothy], [u2 Oz/place, u3 Oz/person]] -- the Wizard's unit-3 facts/cells land on the place cluster. The same_name path (1359-1365) then finds u1 Oz/person but settled(root(u1 Oz), root(u3 Oz)) is true, so no repair. The roster_root fallback (1337-1341) is unreachable since a roster name is always some member's exact name. Violates ruling 28's intent (declared continuation of the entity the roster showed) and writes wrong provenance. Scenario is plausible in this corpus (Oz the Wizard vs Oz the land; a method and its topic in a paper).

confirmed.title: The final sweep decides majorness by the local's flag on one side and the cluster's on the other, so a pair is judged or skipped depending on unit order
confirmed.claim: nominate() classifies `a` by a["major"] (the unit-local salience) but `b` by `rb in major_roots` (cluster membership). In the sweep every local is `a` for the pairs with earlier locals, so a minor local that the judge merged into a major cluster is still treated as a minor when it is the later of the pair, and the pair is dropped as minor-vs-minor even though one side is a rolling major.
confirmed.scenario: Probe: unit 1 `cottage (the little cottage)` (minor), unit 2 `house (Dorothy's house)` (major), unit 3 `house (the little house)` (minor, judged same as unit 2's house). Sweep nominates nothing: cottage stays its own cluster. With the units in the order X, M, Y the same pair is nominated (order 2) and judged. The sweep is meant to judge what the rolling lists never met; a minor local merged into a major cluster earlier in the document is exactly that case, and it is missed whenever it is the later local.
confirmed.fix: In nominate, treat `a` as major when its cluster holds a major: `a_major = a["major"] or ra in major_roots`, and use a_major in the order test.

verdict.reason: Reproduced by exec-ing the notebook blocks as the battery does (notebooks/threadatlas-ingestor.py, nominate() line 1389: `if a["major"] and b_major` / line 1391 `elif a["major"]`; `b_major` at 1388 is cluster-based, `a` is judged by its unit-local flag). Three units, all kind "place": unit 1 `cottage` (unnamed, minor, form "the little house"); unit 2 `house` (named, major, form "Dorothy's house"); unit 3 `house` (named, minor, form "the little house"). unite_on_sight puts house@3 into house@2's cluster (same_name), so major_roots = {that cluster}. The only nominating reason between the clusters is shared_surface between house@3 and cottage@1 (house@2 and cottage share nothing). Result in this order: rolling candidates [] and the sweep (finish(), line 1596: nominate(state, state.locals_, len(state.locals_))) returns [] — the pair is dropped at line 1396 as minor-vs-minor because a=house@3 has a["major"]=False even though its cluster is a rolling major. Reversed order (house-minor@1, house-major@2, cottage@3): the same cluster pair is nominated at unit 3 with order 2, reason shared_surface, and one judge call is made. So whether a major-cluster vs minor-cluster pair is judged depends only on which local came later, and the sweep, whose stated job is to judge what the rolling lists never met, misses exactly this case; a possible union is lost and the package can carry a duplicate entity. Ruling 28 (major vs minor is always set, only minor vs minor never) is violated in this edge. The proposed fix is correct: compute `a_major = a["major"] or ra in major_roots` and use it at 1389/1391. Severity medium stands (order-dependent missed union; occurs in this corpus whenever a later unit's minor mention of an established major is the only surface linking it to an earlier unnamed minor).

confirmed.title: settled() scans every kept_apart and deferred pair with two find() calls per entry on every query; the rolling phase and the sweep grow cubically
confirmed.claim: settled() concatenates the two lists and calls find() twice per entry on each call; it is called from nominate for every candidate local pair (O(fresh x locals) per unit, O(n^2) in the sweep), from judge_pairs per batched pair, and from unite_on_sight. Total cost is (pairs nominated) x (pairs judged so far), and both grow with the document.
confirmed.scenario: Measured with block 8 alone, a stub judge that never says same, 15 locals a unit, ~3% of name pairs sharing a word: rolling 25 units 0.5 s, 50 units 5 s, 75 units 24 s, 100 units (1,500 locals, 14,646 settled pairs) 74 s, then the sweep's nominate 63 s for zero new pairs (23,655 settled() calls). Extrapolated to a 200-unit novel that is on the order of 20 minutes of pure Python per document, on top of the model calls; a 19,206-chat corpus is unaffected (tiny n) but the GraphRAG-Bench novels are not.
confirmed.fix: Index settled pairs by current roots once per query burst: at the top of nominate (and once per batch in judge_pairs) build `apart = {frozenset((find(x), find(y))) for x, y in kept_apart + deferred}` and test `frozenset((ra, rb)) in apart`; or keep kept_apart as a dict root -> set(roots) merged in Clusters.unite.

verdict.reason: Reproduced by exec-ing blocks 1-8 of notebooks/threadatlas-ingestor.py the way the battery does, with a stub judge that always answers "different", 15 named locals a unit (3 majors), two-word names from a 133-word pool (~3% of name pairs share a word), no facts. Rolling.settled (line 1307-1311) builds `self.kept_apart + self.deferred` and calls find() twice per entry on every query, and it is queried from nominate (line 1385, for every candidate pair that passes candidate_reason, including minor-vs-minor pairs since the order check comes after), from judge_pairs (line 1451, per batched pair) and from unite_on_sight (line 1364). Measured: 25 units 0.41 s rolling + 0.40 s finish (705 settled pairs, 2,715 settled() calls); 50 units 4.13 s + 4.40 s (2,806 pairs, 11,005 calls); 100 units 52.2 s rolling + 60.1 s finish (1,500 locals, 11,249 settled pairs, 44,662 + 33,060 settled() calls), and the 100-unit sweep made zero new judge calls (judge_calls stayed at 1,168) for its 60 s. Growth is ~10x per doubling of units, i.e. cubic. The export (data/export/units.jsonl) has a 615-unit document plus documents of 155, 135, 112 units and 17 documents of 50+ units, so the cost lands on this corpus: at 615 units the extrapolated pure-Python time is hours per document. No wrong data is written, so medium stands (wasted time, not a ruling violation). The proposed fix (index settled pairs by current roots once per nominate/batch, or keep kept_apart as root -> set(roots) merged in Clusters.unite) is sound; note that any cached index must be rebuilt after a union since find() results change.

confirmed.title: A resumed document's judged-pair and judge-call counts start at zero, so its completion stats disagree with its ledger
confirmed.claim: replay_rows re-applies the checkpointed verdicts but never increments state.pairs_judged or state.judge_calls, while ingest() carefully carries calls and cost across the resume (calls_before_stop, cost_before). finish() returns state.pairs_judged as n_judged, which goes into stats["judged_pairs"], the completion record, show_reconcile and ingest.log.
confirmed.scenario: Probe D: three units rolled live give pairs_judged 1 with one `judged different` ledger row; the same units replayed from their rolling rows give pairs_judged 0 with the identical ledger. A document that stopped at the spend limit after 20 of 24 chapters and resumed reports only the last four chapters' judged pairs beside a ledger and a calls count that cover all 24.
confirmed.fix: In replay_rows count the replayed judge rows: `state.pairs_judged += sum(1 for row in rows.get("ledger", []) if row["how"] in ("judged", "judged again"))`, and checkpoint judge_calls with the unit's rows (rows["judge_calls"]) so roll_unit can add it back.

verdict.reason: Confirmed by code reading and by executing the notebook blocks. replay_rows (notebooks/threadatlas-ingestor.py lines 1479-1493) re-applies each checkpointed ledger row's verdict (unite / kept_apart / deferred) and appends the row to state.ledger, but never increments state.pairs_judged or state.judge_calls; those are only bumped inside judge_pairs (lines 1458-1459), which replay bypasses by design. finish() (line 1610) returns state.pairs_judged as n_judged; ingest() (line 2421) stores it as stats["judged_pairs"], which write_package writes into the package's document record (line 2009), show() prints and appends to ingest.log (line 2450), and show_reconcile displays. Meanwhile stats["calls"] and stats["cost"] are carried across the resume via calls_before_stop / cost_before (line 2422), so the two figures in the same log line cover different spans. Reproduction (blocks exec'd as the battery does, judge stubbed to answer "different"): three units, unit 2 an unnamed local sharing unit 1's surface. Rolled live: pairs_judged 1, judge_calls 1, ledger [('judged','different')]. Same records replayed from the rows roll_unit returned: pairs_judged 0, judge_calls 0, ledger [('judged','different')]. So a document that stops at the spend limit and resumes writes a package whose stats.judged_pairs counts only the post-resume units' judged pairs (plus the sweep/last look) beside a ledger and a calls count covering the whole document. Severity medium is right: wrong diagnostic count in the package and log, no wrong entities, facts, or provenance. The anchoring line is better placed at replay_rows itself (1479) than at 1505, the call site in roll_unit; the fix sketched by the reviewer (count replayed rows whose how is "judged" or "judged again") is sound, though judge_calls cannot be recovered from ledger rows alone since a batch of up to ten pairs is one call, so it would need checkpointing with the unit's rows as the reviewer suggests, or the watch line's per-unit "judge calls" figure will also read 0 on replay.

confirmed.title: A declared continuation with an unnamed side between two minors is logged as "so judged" but is never set before the judge
confirmed.claim: unite_on_sight writes a candidate ledger row saying the pair is judged, but nominate() then drops it as minor-vs-minor (line 1395), the sweep drops it for the same reason, and the model's explicit declaration is discarded with no record that says so.
confirmed.scenario: Probe C: unit 1 `meeting (the user's meeting)` (minor, unnamed, with a fact, so on the roster); unit 2 lists the same name with continues set. Ledger: `candidate declared ... a side is unnamed, so judged`; the judge is never called; two clusters remain. In a novel this is every unnamed minor the model re-lists across chapters with continues set (the house, the cyclone); their facts then ride into a major only from the cluster that happens to be tied to it.
confirmed.fix: Either let a `declared` candidate through the order gate in nominate (a continuation the model declared is stronger evidence than a shared word, and ruling 28 only forbids the on-sight union), or write the row honestly: `not set: minor against minor`.

verdict.reason: Reproduced by exec-ing Block 8 with a stubbed generate: unit 1 has unnamed minor "meeting (the user's meeting)" with one fact; unit 2 lists the same name, unnamed, minor, with continues set. unite_on_sight (notebooks/threadatlas-ingestor.py:1355-1356) appends a ledger row "candidate / declared / ... a side is unnamed, so judged". nominate() computes reason "declared" (line 1215) but the order gate at lines 1395-1396 drops the pair because neither side's root is a major, so state.candidates stays empty and no pair is returned; judge() is never called (zero stub calls). finish() reuses nominate with the same gate, so the sweep drops it again and deferred is empty; the result is two clusters for the same declared entity. A control with the unit-1 local as major reached judge(), showing the gate is the only difference. Ruling 28 permits never setting minors against minors, so the dropped union is arguably by design, but the ledger row records "so judged" for a pair that is never judged nor scored, and the model's explicit declaration leaves no honest trace. Low severity: wrong diagnostic plus a split cluster for unnamed minors re-declared across units (their about-facts then ride into a major only from the cluster tied to it). Fix: either write the row as not set (minor against minor) or let a declared candidate through the order gate.

confirmed.title: The `continues` field is validated by exact string match against the roster, so a name the model writes loosely loses the declared union
confirmed.claim: derive_unit keeps e["continues"] only when it is exactly in roster_names; a leading article, different case or collapsed whitespace turns it into None, and the pair falls to nominate's shared_surface path and a Terra judge call, or to nothing when both are minors. Stage A added loose_name precisely because the model writes listed names back loosely (33 facts lost to "The Scarecrow"), but the same laxity was not applied where it feeds block 8's declared path.
confirmed.scenario: Roster line `- The Scarecrow (person; ...)`; the model returns continues "the Scarecrow" (or "Scarecrow"). continues becomes None, the entity is treated as new to the document, and the union that ruling 28 says happens on sight costs a judge call instead; on a chat corpus of 19,206 documents each such miss is a Terra call.
confirmed.fix: Match continues the way facts are matched: build `listed = {loose_name(n): n for n in roster_names}` and set `continues = listed.get(loose_name(e.get("continues") or ""))`.

verdict.reason: Reproduced by reading and by running the gate. notebooks/threadatlas-ingestor.py:1013 is `continues = e.get("continues") if e.get("continues") in roster_names else None` where roster_names (line 986) is the exact set of roster names. With roster {"The Scarecrow"}, the values "the Scarecrow", "Scarecrow" and "The  Scarecrow" all become None (checked with a two-line Python run). The drop is silent: no dropped_entities row, no diagnostic, so the declared continuation vanishes from rec["entities"] and from everything block 8 replays from the checkpoint. Downstream the gate is stricter than its own consumers: continued() (line 1331-1335) and candidate_reason() (line 1215) compare with norm(), so a case or whitespace variant would have matched there had it survived line 1013; only the exact-match gate loses it. Minimal failure: unit 2 establishes "The Scarecrow" (person, named); unit 5 returns an entity named "Scarecrow" with continues "the Scarecrow". continues -> None; unite_on_sight's same_name path needs norm(name) equality, which "scarecrow" vs "the scarecrow" fails; so instead of the on-sight union ruling 28 prescribes for two named sides, the pair is nominated by shared_surface and spends a Terra judge call, and if both locals are minor it is never nominated at all (minor vs minor is excluded), so the minor's facts stay split across two clusters. The model writing listed names loosely is not hypothetical for this corpus: the file's own loose_name docstring (line 530-533) records that "The Scarecrow" and "Dainty China Country" came back as "the Scarecrow" and "the Dainty China Country" in the fact stage, which is why loose_name was added for subject/object resolution; the same laxity was not applied to continues. Severity low as claimed: cost is a wasted judge call or a missed minor union, not wrong data written outright. The proposed fix (map loose_name(roster name) -> roster name and look continues up through loose_name) is consistent with how facts are resolved and with the norm()-based consumers.

confirmed.title: A spend stop (or any worker error) in the document-level stage throws away every finished Terra result, and the resume repays the whole stage
confirmed.claim: The sidecar checkpoints unit records only. The sweep and last-look judge calls in finish(), the fold, the embedding, the entity abstracts (in_parallel at line 1752) and the adjudications (in_parallel here) exist only in memory until write_package. When call() raises SpendStop at line 405 inside one worker, or one worker raises RuntimeError after three 429/5xx replies, list(pool.map) propagates the first exception in item order and discards every result already computed; the WORKERS-1 calls in flight still run to completion and are billed past SPEND_STOP (the stop is checked only before a call starts); ingest() unwinds writing nothing. On the next run checkpointed() replays the units and every document-level call is made again. The sidecar docstring at lines 1784-1785 ('a stop mid-document costs only the unit that was running') and the note at line 2490 ('its finished units are checkpointed') describe the cheapest part of the document; adjudication and the entity abstracts are the Terra-priced bulk of a book's spend.
confirmed.scenario: Oz book 1 with SPEND_STOP=5.00 (block 13): the stop is crossed while adjudication 30 of 38 is in flight. Worker A's next call() raises SpendStop; workers B, C, D finish their adjudications (three more Terra calls logged to calls.jsonl after the stop); the 29 finished adjudications, all 38 entity-abstract folds, the abstract fold, the embed and the sweep/last-look judge calls (on the order of $2-4) are logged as spent and dropped. The next session resumes from 26 unit rows, re-judges the sweep (a Terra call per ten pairs), re-folds, re-abstracts and re-adjudicates all 38 majors. The same happens for a single non-stop failure: one adjudication returning 429 three times fails the whole document (run() notes ERROR, continues) and the resume repays the stage.
confirmed.fix: Checkpoint document-level results in the sidecar as they land, keyed so replay can skip the call: the sweep/last-look ledger rows after finish(), the abstract and each entity abstract, and each adjudication result keyed by entity index (write the row under LOG_LOCK from the worker, or iterate as_completed and append per result), then have checkpointed() hand them back and adjudicate()/fold_document() skip majors already held. At minimum, correct the docstring and the run() note so the owner knows a stop after the last unit repays the sweep, fold, abstracts and adjudications.

verdict.reason: Reproduced by exec-ing the notebook blocks with the battery's scripted model (WORKERS=4) on Oz 01_55 and raising SpendStop inside the second adjudicate call. Observed: run returns done=0, no package written, the sidecar holds all 24 unit recs and only the keys ['calls','cost','flags','rec','triage'] (append_sidecar is called only at ingest() lines ~2373 and ~2401; nothing between the unit loop and write_package at line 2431 checkpoints). Document-level calls completed and then discarded in the stopped run: judge (sweep) 1, fold 1, entity_abstract 3, adjudicate 2; two adjudicate calls were logged to CALLS after the stop was raised (the in-flight workers ran to completion because in_parallel's list(pool.map) at line 339 raises the first exception only after the with-block waits on the pool, and the SPEND_STOP check at line 405 runs only before a call starts). The resume then repaid every one of them: judge 1, fold 1, entity_abstract 3, adjudicate 3, predicates 1 (embed is lost too in a real run; the stub bypasses call()). The docstring at lines 1784-1785 ('a stop mid-document costs only the unit that was running') and the note at line 2490 are false for a stop after the last unit, which on a novel is where the Terra-priced bulk is spent. Not a ruling violation (audit line 51 promises only unit-level resume), so medium stands: wasted calls and misleading diagnostics on a real corpus document.

confirmed.title: A resumed document's completion under-reports its cost and calls: only the unit rows are summed
confirmed.claim: stats['cost'] and stats['calls'] add cost_before and calls_before_stop from checkpointed(), which sums row.get('cost')/row.get('calls') over the 'rec' rows only (lines 2075-2079). The triage row written at line 2374 carries no cost or calls, so the triage call is never counted on a resumed document, and nothing the stopped attempt spent at document level (sweep and last-look judge calls, fold, embed, entity abstracts, adjudications, predicate judge) is recorded anywhere the resume can read. The completion record, the manifest row (line 2486), show() and receipt()['cost_of_packages'] all inherit the low number, so the receipt's per-package cost no longer reconciles with calls.jsonl.
confirmed.scenario: The stop of the previous finding: the first attempt logs ~$5 for Oz book 1 in calls.jsonl; the resumed attempt spends ~$3.5 on the document-level stage and writes a completion whose stats.cost is 26 unit costs + $3.5 (about $5.5) while calls.jsonl rows with doc == that source_uri sum to about $8.5. receipt.json's cost_of_packages is short by the stopped attempt's document-level spend for every document that was resumed, and every resumed document also loses its triage call from stats.calls.
confirmed.fix: Write cost and calls into the triage row and into a per-stage sidecar row (or one 'document_stage' row) as each document-level stage ends, and sum those in checkpointed(); or derive a document's cost and calls at write time from the calls.jsonl rows whose doc field equals the source_uri, which is already the ground truth.

verdict.reason: Reproduced against the notebook with the battery's stub model (exec of the blocks the way test_ingestor.py does). Scenario: graphrag-bench/Novel-40700.txt (two unit kinds, so triage fires); the first attempt is stopped by a SpendStop inside the adjudication stage after all 8 units were checkpointed. calls.jsonl for that doc then holds 37 calls / $0.037 (triage 1, unit calls, judge 5, fold 1, entity_abstract 3, adjudicate 3), but checkpointed() at lines 2075-2079 sums only the 'rec' rows: 29 calls / $0.029. confirmed.title: Calls, retries and rejections from the parallel stages cannot be attributed to a major
confirmed.claim: adjudicate_one passes the document ctx ({'doc': uri}) to generate(), and abstract_of at line 1747 does the same, so calls.jsonl, retries.jsonl and rejections.jsonl rows for 'adjudicate' and 'entity_abstract' carry only the document. Before stage D the sequential order let a reader line a row up with the major; with four workers interleaving, the order in the logs is arrival order and says nothing. retries.jsonl was added (audit ruling 26) precisely to explain '38 adjudications took 70 calls', and it now cannot name the major. A reply rejected twice returns None and adjudicate_one records nothing about it: result['dropped'] stays 0, result['skipped'] stays None, so a major with dozens of landed facts and an empty adjudicated record is indistinguishable in the package from one Terra consolidated to nothing.
confirmed.scenario: Oz book 1: two adjudications miss the schema twice (the null-value attribute shape that ruling 26 mentions). rejections.jsonl holds two rows {stage: adjudicate, category: schema, doc: .../oz/01_55.txt}; calls.jsonl shows the four calls scattered among the other workers' rows; the package has no adjudicated_fact/attribute rows for those two majors and counts.adjudication_dropped is 0. Nothing identifies which two majors were lost.
confirmed.fix: Pass ctx={**ctx, 'entity': e['name']} (and first_unit or index) in adjudicate_one and abstract_of so every logged row names the major; when generate() returns None in adjudicate_one set result['rejected'] = True and count it in the completion (e.g. adjudications_rejected) beside adjudications_skipped.

verdict.reason: Reproduced by exec-ing the notebook blocks the way the battery does and driving the real generate() with a call() stub that misses ADJUDICATE_SCHEMA twice. adjudicate() at line 2170 passes the document ctx ({'doc': uri}) unchanged, as does abstract_of -> fold() at line 1747, so the rows written to calls.jsonl, retries.jsonl and rejections.jsonl for stages 'adjudicate' and 'entity_abstract' carry only {stage, category, detail, doc}: the repro's rows are exactly {'stage': 'adjudicate', 'category': 'schema', 'detail': 'SchemaError: $.attributes: missing', 'doc': 'oz/01.txt'} with no entity, and with in_parallel (WORKERS=4) interleaving the calls the log order no longer stands in for the major. confirmed.title: Resuming from the sidecar drops the triage flags

A resumed document therefore writes stats.triage_flags = [] and show_triage prints no FLAG lines even though the first attempt recorded, for example, 'triage named a kind the document does not have' or 'triage reply rejected twice; every kind was read'.

verdict.reason: Confirmed by reading notebooks/threadatlas-ingestor.py. append_sidecar (line 2374) writes {"triage": excluded, "flags": flags} as the sidecar's first row, but checkpointed() (line 2072) returns only rows[0]["triage"] and never reads rows[0]["flags"]. ingest() sets flags = [] at line 2368 and reassigns it only inside the fresh-triage branch (line 2373), so on the resume path (excluded is not None) flags stays []. That empty list reaches show_triage at line 2383 (no FLAG lines) and stats["triage_flags"] at line 2422, which write_package embeds in the completion record (line 2007, "stats": stats). Scenario: a document whose triage reply was rejected twice (flag appended at line 2096) is stopped after some units; the next session resumes it and the package's stats.triage_flags is [] and no FLAG prints, so the record that triage never happened for this document is lost. Only a diagnostic field is affected, no facts or provenance, so low is the right severity. Fix as proposed: have checkpointed() return rows[0].get("flags", []) and assign it to flags on the resume path.

confirmed.title: Chained predicate merges are applied one hop, leaving facts under a predicate the judge retired
confirmed.claim: judge_predicates builds out['map'] as raw -> target one merge at a time.
